## Site Energy and Sustainability Review 2025

Group EHS

## 1. Introduction

This review summarises energy-saving projects and emissions at each manufacturing site. Absolute consumption figures are reported in the Annual Operations Report; this document reports savings and renewable capacity only.

## 2. Tampere Works (Finland)

Tampere Works reduced its energy consumption by 2,600 MWh (7.1%) compared with FY2024, mainly through compressed-air leak repairs.

Rooftop solar capacity at Tampere Works reached 570 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 5,890 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Tampere Works is Sofia Etxeberria.

## 3. Gdansk Assembly (Poland)

Gdansk Assembly reduced its energy consumption by 2,050 MWh (8.7%) compared with FY2024, mainly through LED lighting retrofits.

Rooftop solar capacity at Gdansk Assembly reached 890 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 5,790 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Gdansk Assembly is Freja Laine.

## 4. Porto Foundry (Portugal)

Porto Foundry reduced its energy consumption by 1,330 MWh (12.6%) compared with FY2024, mainly through process cooling optimisation.

Rooftop solar capacity at Porto Foundry reached 1,130 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 8,740 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Porto Foundry is Nadia Mendes.

## 5. Brno Machining (Czechia)

Brno Machining reduced its energy consumption by 2,980 MWh (4.5%) compared with FY2024, mainly through weekend shutdown discipline.

Rooftop solar capacity at Brno Machining reached 770 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 7,820 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Brno Machining is Aleksi Kowalski.

## 6. Lyon Systems (France)

Lyon Systems reduced its energy consumption by 2,850 MWh (5.3%) compared with FY2024, mainly through variable-speed drives on fans.

Rooftop solar capacity at Lyon Systems reached 1,000 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 3,470 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Lyon Systems is Zofia Salo.

## 7. Bilbao Plant (Spain)

Bilbao Plant reduced its energy consumption by 1,405 MWh (3.1%) compared with FY2024, mainly through a new building management system.

Rooftop solar capacity at Bilbao Plant reached 710 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 8,770 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Bilbao Plant is Otto Girard.

## 8. Graz Electronics (Austria)

Graz Electronics reduced its energy consumption by 2,580 MWh (7.2%) compared with FY2024, mainly through boiler replacement.

Rooftop solar capacity at Graz Electronics reached 870 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 1,340 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Graz Electronics is Elena Kowalski.

## 9. Aarhus Service Centre (Denmark)

Aarhus Service Centre reduced its energy consumption by 2,475 MWh (10.5%) compared with FY2024, mainly through furnace heat recovery.

Rooftop solar capacity at Aarhus Service Centre reached 1,290 kWp. Scope 2 emissions for the site were 12,920 tonnes CO2e.

The energy manager responsible for Aarhus Service Centre is Ida Virtanen.
